subject: english-studies
title: Singular and plural
summary: Change a naming word from one to more than one, including the tricky ones.

lesson.text: A singular noun names one thing: a book. A plural noun names more than one: books.
Ending in s, x, ch or sh: add -es
But if a vowel comes before the y, just add -s: boy → boys, day → days, key → keys.
Special plurals to learn by heart

items: man → men, woman → women, child → children
tooth → teeth, foot → feet, mouse → mice
sheep → sheep, fish → fish (they stay the same)

lesson.title: Make it plural: one lady, one tomato
steps: Lady ends in a consonant + y: lady → ladies.
Tomato ends in o and adds -es: tomato → tomatoes (like potato → potatoes).

lesson.text: Say the plural out loud. If it sounds like an extra syllable (box-es, bus-es), it usually needs -es.

questions.explanation: Box ends in x, so add -es: boxes.
Child is a special plural: children. "Childrens" is wrong because children is already plural.
City ends in a consonant (t) + y, so change y to -ies: cities.
Tooth becomes teeth. The others should be feet, sheep and mice.
A vowel (e) comes before the y, so just add -s: keys. Only consonant + y changes to -ies.
